tasks.task: Write a press release a reporter can use in a minute

items.when: Before writing, when you are not sure the news is a story a reporter would run
When the news is confirmed and you need headline, five Ws, checked facts and quotes
When the headline is flat, to get several factual angles and pick the plainest strong one
When the release runs long, to cut it and keep a log of what went
When the release is drafted, to list the hard questions it raises and answer them first
When the draft is full of 'delighted' and 'leading', to put it in plain exact words
Before the release goes out, to trace every figure, date, name and quote to a source the client holds

tasks.task: Find the story angle in a piece of business news

items.when: When past releases got no coverage and you need an honest test of this one
When the news seems plain, to get product and story angles ranked against each other
When you need what people have said on the topic lately, to tie the news to it
When the one-line story is forgettable, to get three versions people will repeat
When the story is true but nobody would pass it on, to find what makes it worth sharing

tasks.task: Build a small media list and pitch each reporter

items.when: When one story needs a short researched list and a personal pitch for each name
When you start from the news alone and need a first list, pitches and a press kit outline
Before the list, to map the sites, shows and newsletters the client's buyers follow
When you must read what a reporter wrote lately, with links, before you write to them
When pitches go unopened, to try subject lines from several angles
Before sending, to test each claim in the pitch and the legal basics of the email

tasks.task: Write one pitch and follow-up for a named reporter or host

items.when: When you have a story and one named reporter, editor, newsletter writer or host
When there is no reply, to write a follow-up that brings a new reason, not a nudge
When the pitch pushes for a yes, to try a version where a no still helps you
Before sending, to test what the pitch says about the outlet against its own pages

tasks.task: Run a news announcement from story to coverage

items.when: Two to four weeks before a launch, hire, partnership or result can be made public
When the launch should win press before any ad money is spent
When two firms announce together and need one message brief and an approval tracker
When you want a second plan with three key messages and a release outline to compare
When the announcement also needs posts written for each social platform
Before the news goes out, to prepare answers to what customers and staff will ask

tasks.task: Build a response pack for a live crisis

items.when: When something has gone wrong that customers, staff or reporters know about or soon will
When you have confirmed facts and need the fact log, statement, notes, Q&A and update plan
When the issue is an outage and you need first notice, progress updates and the all-clear
When you must decide who hears first and how, to map everyone the issue touches
Before anything is sent, to split what is confirmed from what is guessed or hoped
When the draft protects the firm first, to start again from the people affected

tasks.task: Write a holding statement in the first hours

items.when: When you must say something true and useful before all the facts are known
When the statement mixes facts with guesses, to mark every line that is not confirmed
When the statement makes promises, to check each one can be kept
When the statement hides behind 'an issue was identified', to say plainly what happened
Before the statement is issued, to keep only facts with a confirmed source and cut the rest

tasks.task: Tell staff and customers before the public hears

items.when: When the staff note and customer message must match the statement word for word on facts
When staff need the news first, with manager talking points and a rollout order
When customers are owed an apology that owns the mistake and says what happens next
When each group gets its own message, to find where the versions contradict each other
When replies to upset customers are drafted, to check promises and tone before sending

tasks.task: Write a crisis communications playbook before one is needed

items.when: When the client has no plan and needs severity levels, roles and ready templates
When you plan for a defect or failure and need who to tell and what to do for 30 days
When the plan must cover staff: who does what and the first-hour message to employees
Before the playbook, to list every group that would need to hear and who owns each
When scenarios are drafted, to test each with the questions a reporter would ask

tasks.task: Review a crisis afterwards and plan the recovery

items.when: When the issue is over and you need a blame-free timeline, causes and follow-ups
When you need reviews, ratings and mentions gathered to see what the crisis left behind
When you need what people are still saying, grouped by theme with notable posts
When the recovery needs a 30-day plan of who to contact and what to put right

tasks.task: Prepare a spokesperson for a media or podcast interview

items.when: Before a spokesperson talks to a reporter or host, in good times or in a crisis
When there are no agreed key messages, to set them with a proof point for each
When the prep sheet is drafted, to add the questions the speaker hopes nobody asks
When a key message is long and abstract, to get three versions that can be said aloud

tasks.task: Set key messages and proof points for the business

items.when: When the client needs a short set of messages with proof for each audience
Before you write, to see what rivals already say so the client does not echo them
When a message is accurate but dull, to get three more memorable versions
When the firm tells press, staff and investors different things, to find the clashes

tasks.task: Write an award entry to the category criteria

items.when: When you have the category, its entry rules and the client's results to hand
When you must choose the category and line up evidence against each criterion first
When the entry rests on a customer result, to outline the case and list evidence gaps
When the entry is over the word limit, to name the main point and cut what fights it
When the entry is a list of numbers, to find one true incident that makes judges care
Before the entry is submitted, to match each result and number claimed to evidence the judges could ask for
When the entry is drafted, so a fresh reader scores it against the category criteria as a judge would

tasks.task: Build a scored calendar of awards and events to enter

items.when: When the client asks which awards and stages are worth the time this year
Before scoring, to find the events and shows the client's buyers really attend or follow
When you need entry dates, fees and rules checked on each organiser's own page

tasks.task: Write a conference talk proposal

items.when: When an event has a call for speakers and the proposal must sell one clear takeaway
Before the abstract, to outline the talk so it builds belief step by step
When the talk title is flat, to get several title angles for the programme
When the outline is drafted, to check the room knows the stakes early
When the title is chosen, to check it picks the right audience and promises a clear gain

tasks.task: Get a client ready to guest on podcasts

items.when: When you need target show rules, a guest one-sheet and pitches for a shortlist of shows
When you write to one named host and must show you know the show and its listeners
When there is no shortlist yet, to find the shows the client's buyers listen to
When the guest cannot say what they do briefly, to get 10, 30 and 60 second versions
Before a booked episode, to prepare the stories, likely questions and what not to say

tasks.task: Write bios, a one-sheet and press kit text

items.when: When a spokesperson, speaker, author or artist needs a press-ready bio in three lengths
When the press kit needs the company's origin story told in a human way
When the founder's story is long, to map it and cut it to the parts that move a reader
When reporters will look the speaker up and the profile must match the new bio
When a bio says 'passionate' and 'visionary', to test it and get a true rewrite

tasks.task: Write an artist press kit and booking pitches

items.when: When an act needs short, medium and long bios for a press kit and programme
When you pitch one named venue booker, promoter or music writer
When the act needs a one-sheet for a release or a pitch for a festival slot
When a booker has not replied, to follow up with a new reason each time
When the kit sounds hyped, to make each line clear, true and easy to picture

tasks.task: Plan the month's earned media work

items.when: In the last week of each month, to plan next month's stories, pitches and entries
When press is untested for this client, to frame it as one small test with a decision rule
When ordinary news is thin, to consider a stunt or gesture people would talk about
When coverage should also earn links and brand mentions for the client's site
When you need this month's talking points in the client's field to react to

tasks.task: Answer journalist requests for expert comment

items.when: When you have a batch of reporter requests and need ranked picks and expert answers
When the reply needs a one-line credit for the expert
Before the comment is sent, to mark which lines are fact and which are opinion

tasks.task: Draft an opinion piece or expert article under a client's name

items.when: When the article is meant to build trust with slow, careful business buyers
When the argument is agreed and you need a full draft with an opening and a close
When an editor needs a headline, to offer several angles without clickbait
When the piece argues three things at once, to name the one idea and cut the rest
Before it goes to an editor, to check each claim is marked as fact or as the author's view

tasks.task: Turn survey or company data into a news story

items.when: When you have survey results and need findings you can defend to a reporter
Before any number is pitched, to see how far the survey's answers can be trusted
When the headline claim is drafted, to test what the data really shows
When the findings hold up and need writing as a release with the method stated
When one number looks striking, to slow down and ask what it counts and against what

tasks.task: Track mentions and report what the coverage did

items.when: When you need mentions, reviews and ratings from many sites gathered in one report
When you need what people said about the news, grouped by theme
When the client asks whether AI tools now mention the brand after the coverage
When you choose which outlets to pitch next, to see which sites AI tools keep citing
When the client needs wins, misses and next steps written up as a monthly report

always.when: Before any release, statement or entry goes out, to check each claim against sources
When copy says 'first', 'best' or 'only', to sort each claim as fine, needs proof or cut
Before anything is sent to a reporter, to catch typos and names spelt two ways

helpers.when: When an accepted talk or a statement read aloud needs a full script
When a crisis or big announcement needs a full staff rollout, not one note
When the issue lives in reviews and search results and needs replies and clean-up
When the news needs a social plan and someone to handle replies after it lands
When a client needs a run of articles or a long piece in their own voice
When the aim of the coverage is links and search ranking, not only awareness

gaps: No library item writes an award entry to scoring criteria or scores a list of awards by fit, cost and odds
No library item writes a conference talk proposal for a call for speakers; the talk items are for student or research talks
No library item covers podcast guesting: scoring shows, a guest one-sheet or a pitch to a host
No library item writes speaker, author or artist bios
No library item covers music publicity: press kit text, booking pitches, release one-sheets, tech and hospitality riders
No library item builds a media list of named reporters from their recent work, or handles embargoes and exclusives
No library item writes a holding statement, recall notice or public data incident notice; the privacy items only check law by country
No library item drills a spokesperson with hostile questions or scores practice answers
No library item reports press coverage: a coverage log, reach, share of voice and whether key messages came through
No library item builds a press page or press kit for the client's site
No library item reviews a finished release or pitch the way a reporter would and scores it
No library item plans a press event, launch invite or media briefing
